73d5dbb18192.title: JWST finds early galaxies may be 4 times more massive than thought
73d5dbb18192.summary: Astronomers using JWST have discovered that massive early galaxies contain far more small, faint stars than expected. That hidden population could make some of these galaxies three to four times more massive than previous estimates. The finding makes it even harder to explain how enormous, mature galaxies formed so soon after the Big Bang. It could also suggest that planets around low-mass stars were more common in the early universe than scientists realized.

That rapid rotation could explain both the fading flares and how the stars ended up in such extraordinarily tight black hole orbits.

Many of the proteins affected by sprinting were also associated with lower risks of obesity, type 2 diabetes, and other metabolic diseases.
